headline: A +31% volume jump over four weeks is landing well — easy-run HR has dropped meaningfully, suggesting the additional load is being absorbed rather than accumulated as fatigue.
confidence_reasons: Multiple data sources active in last 3 days
summary:
The volume increase this block is substantial by any measure, and the aerobic response is the key signal here: your easy-run heart rate has fallen noticeably compared to the prior period at comparable efforts and paces. That's the kind of efficiency gain you'd expect to see when a training load increase is being handled well — not suppressed by fatigue. The June 27th threshold session stands apart as the hardest effort of the recent period, and the three runs since have all been appropriately controlled in intensity. The pattern reads as a well-structured load-and-absorb sequence.

Your running streak has matched its all-time best at 20 weeks, and strength volume has held steady across both blocks. The combination of rising mileage, maintained strength work, and improving aerobic efficiency at easy paces is about as positive a multi-metric picture as this data can offer.

The one thing worth naming plainly: a +31% four-week jump is meaningful, and while the HR data suggests absorption is going well so far, the next few weeks will reveal whether that adaptation is consolidating or whether cumulative fatigue starts to surface. The data supports continuing to push — but this is the window to pay attention to.
watch_items: Monitor whether easy-run HR continues its downward trend or begins to creep back up as cumulative load adds up
Watch for any change in how the legs feel on back-to-back run days — durability across consecutive efforts is a key signal at this volume
The 20-week streak milestone is a natural inflection point; notice whether motivation and freshness remain high or whether any subtle staleness is emerging
Strength consistency has held well through a volume spike — worth tracking whether session quality holds as weekly mileage stays elevated

evidence_items.text: ▲ 4-week volume 163 km vs 125 km prior block (+31%)
▼ Easy-run HR averaging 145 bpm vs 157 bpm prior period (comparable-effort runs, 8 vs 6 runs)
